strings.data.compatMatrix.comparativeAnalytical: The comparative level works reliably with any method. The analytical method ensures maximal formal rigor.
strings.data.compatMatrix.comparativeCreative: The comparative level works reliably with any method. The creative method gives the most original and unexpected results.
strings.data.compatMatrix.comparativeDeconstruct: The comparative level works reliably with any method. The deconstructive method makes it possible to uncover the hidden premises of each tradition.
strings.data.compatMatrix.comparativeDialectical: The comparative level works reliably with any method. The dialectical method gives the most structured result at this level.
strings.data.compatMatrix.comparativeHermeneutic: The comparative level works reliably with any method. The hermeneutic method gives the most contextually rich result.
strings.data.compatMatrix.comparativeIntegrative: The comparative level works reliably with any method. The integrative method is optimal for finding common grounds between traditions.
strings.data.compatMatrix.generativeAnalyticalAd: Choose it when the synthesis claims genuine novelty and must prove it formally; for an audience oriented toward the analytic tradition.
strings.data.compatMatrix.generativeAnalyticalTe: Growing synergy. The generative level claims non-derivability from the traditions — the analytical method provides a formal apparatus to prove it. Synergy peaks (★★★) are in the theses and critique, where the claims need verification.
strings.data.compatMatrix.generativeCreativeAdvi: For the most experimental syntheses, when the value lies in posing new questions rather than in a closed system.
strings.data.compatMatrix.generativeCreativeOrde: The genetic order strengthens the synergy: an open dialogue generates questions, the creative method maps them. The most organic sequence for this pair.
strings.data.compatMatrix.generativeCreativeText: Peaks in the open sections. Both parameters refuse a closed ending: the level gropes for the contours of a new language, the method produces a map of questions. The only combination where both parameters explicitly do not require a completed synthesis.
strings.data.compatMatrix.generativeDeconstructi: Choose it for the most ambitious syntheses with high claims to originality, when the concept seed formulates a problem that none of the philosophers could pose within their own system.

Maximal critical potential. Both parameters share one epistemological gesture — revealing what is not visible from inside existing systems. “Blind spot” (the level) = “unrecognized premise” (the method). The only pair where both axes independently require proving that the result cannot be derived.
strings.data.compatMatrix.generativeDialecticalA: It is recommended to add an instruction to the “Additional context” field: “Interpret the limitations of the traditions as dialectical poles, and the generated category as sublation.” This instruction is passed to the model via p.ctx before each section.
strings.data.compatMatrix.generativeDialecticalO: The genetic order reduces the tension: the problem is articulated in the dialogue, and the philosophers' limitations appear as thesis/antithesis organically rather than by the prompt's prescription.
strings.data.compatMatrix.generativeDialecticalT: Manageable tension. The tension is reconcilable on condition that “the limitation of philosopher A” = thesis, “the limitation of philosopher B” = antithesis, “the generated category” = sublation. This is a non-trivial reinterpretation of dialectical roles, which the prompt does not prescribe explicitly.
strings.data.compatMatrix.generativeHermeneuticA: Better avoided. If the hermeneutic method is essential, lower the level to comparative or transformative.
strings.data.compatMatrix.generativeHermeneuticO: The conflict is less acute than with the generative level, but it is still not recommended.
The genetic order slightly softens the conflict: hermeneutic understanding forms more naturally in dialogue. The structural contradiction (horizons vs. the problem) remains.
strings.data.compatMatrix.generativeHermeneuticT: Systemic conflict. The hermeneutic method organizes the graph around the horizons of the traditions, whereas the generative level forbids building categories from traditions. Four key sections receive incompatible criteria for organizing the content.
strings.data.compatMatrix.generativeIntegrativeT: The maximal conflict of the matrix. The generative level builds categories from the problem, not from traditions; the integrative method requires building from the traditions' common grounds. The mutual exclusion is total — a conflict in 5 of 6 key sections.
strings.data.compatMatrix.transformativeAnalytic: Choose it when you need transformative depth with analytical rigor and a formal proof of emergence.

The genetic order strengthens the synergy: tensions are discovered in the dialogue, and the analytical apparatus then verifies the emergence of the categories that actually arose, rather than fitting them after the fact.
Productive paradox. The analytical method makes the claims of the transformative level verifiable: “emergence” ceases to be a narrative assertion and becomes the result of a formal audit of premises.
strings.data.compatMatrix.transformativeCreative: Choose it when freedom in establishing relations between the transformed categories matters; for syntheses in an experimental context.
The genetic order strengthens the synergy: creative combinatorics feeds on the surprises of the dialogue. With the architectural order, creativity is reduced to decorating a predefined framework.

Productive paradox. The transformative level creates categories with undetermined relations. The creative method's permission to mark relations as hypothetical is not a weakness but an honest ontology of the new.
strings.data.compatMatrix.transformativeDeconstr: Choose it when philosophical honesty toward the sources matters and when the synthesis must show why the source systems could not reach the result on their own.

Structural resonance. “Tension between systems” (the level) arises exactly where their hidden premises are incompatible (the method). Transformation = deconstruction + reassembly. A built-in self-check mechanism.
strings.data.compatMatrix.transformativeDialecti: The ideal choice when the philosophers form clear oppositions and the result must be both historically grounded and logically necessary.

Structural resonance. Both parameters share one ontological gesture — productive conflict as a source of the new. The “tension” of the level = the thesis↔antithesis pair of the method. “The birth of the new from impossibility” = sublation. Two languages for one process.
strings.data.compatMatrix.transformativeHermeneu: If the “Dialogue” section is excluded, the tension drops to a manageable ≈. If the dialogue is included, changing the method is recommended.

The genetic order slightly softens the conflict: the hermeneutic circle works more naturally when understanding expands in dialogue before formalization. The conflict of endings (expansion vs. rupture) remains.

Moderate conflict. The transformative level builds on incompatibility (the birth of the new from impossibility), the hermeneutic method — on the expansion of horizons (growing compatibility). The conflict is concentrated in the “Dialogue” section, where the two endings are incompatible.
strings.data.compatMatrix.transformativeIntegrat: Hard contradiction. The transformative level builds on incompatibility as the source of the new; the integrative method — on common grounds as the source. These are mutually exclusive ontologies of synthesis. The conflict affects 5 of 6 key sections.
strings.data.taxonomy.abductiveDesc: Inference to the best explanation of what is observed
strings.data.taxonomy.aestheticDesc: Categories of the beautiful, of art and of the perception of forms
strings.data.taxonomy.analogyDesc: Structural or functional similarity of the categories
strings.data.taxonomy.analyticalDesc: Categories of conceptual analysis, clarity and argumentation
strings.data.taxonomy.anthropologicalDesc: Categories of the human being, its nature and existence
strings.data.taxonomy.axiologicalDesc: Categories of values and their hierarchies
strings.data.taxonomy.causalDesc: A cause-and-effect relation: one category produces or conditions another
strings.data.taxonomy.complementarityDesc: The categories complement each other into a whole
strings.data.taxonomy.conceptualDesc: A semantic link between notions within a conceptual network
strings.data.taxonomy.concretizationDesc: A particular case or instance of a general category
strings.data.taxonomy.conjunctiveDesc: Joint action: the categories work only together
strings.data.taxonomy.contradictionDesc: The categories are incompatible or mutually negate each other
strings.data.taxonomy.deductiveDesc: Logical derivation of the particular from the general
strings.data.taxonomy.definingDesc: One category is part of the definition of another
strings.data.taxonomy.developmentDesc: One category is an unfolded stage of the becoming of another
strings.data.taxonomy.dialecticalDesc: A relation through contradiction and its sublation: thesis–antithesis–synthesis
strings.data.taxonomy.disjunctiveDesc: A relation of exclusive or alternating alternatives
strings.data.taxonomy.emergenceDesc: A new quality arises from the interaction of the source categories
strings.data.taxonomy.epistemologicalDesc: Categories of cognition, knowledge and its justification
strings.data.taxonomy.ethicalDesc: Categories of morality, of what ought to be, of good and evil
strings.data.taxonomy.existentialDesc: Categories of existence, freedom and finitude
strings.data.taxonomy.foundingDesc: One category founds another, serves as its ground
strings.data.taxonomy.generalizationDesc: A transition from a particular category to a more general one
strings.data.taxonomy.hermeneuticalDesc: Categories of understanding, interpretation and tradition
strings.data.taxonomy.hierarchicalDesc: A relation of subordination: a more general category includes a particular one
strings.data.taxonomy.identityDesc: The categories coincide in content while differing in expression
strings.data.taxonomy.inductiveDesc: A generalizing inference from particular cases to the general
strings.data.taxonomy.interdisciplinaryDesc: Categories at the intersection of philosophy and other disciplines
strings.data.taxonomy.linguisticDesc: Categories of language, meaning and sign systems
strings.data.taxonomy.logicalDesc: Categories of forms of thought, inference and entailment
strings.data.taxonomy.manifestationDesc: One category is a manifestation or expression of another
strings.data.taxonomy.meansEndDesc: One category serves as a means of achieving another
strings.data.taxonomy.metaphysicalDesc: Categories of first principles and ultimate foundations of reality
strings.data.taxonomy.necessaryConditionDesc: Without the first category the second is impossible
strings.data.taxonomy.ontologicalDesc: Categories of being, of what is, and of modes of existence
strings.data.taxonomy.partWholeDesc: A mereological relation: a category is a component of another
strings.data.taxonomy.phenomenologicalDesc: Categories of the experience of consciousness, givenness and intentionality
strings.data.taxonomy.politicalDesc: Categories of power, the state and social order
strings.data.taxonomy.practicalDesc: Categories of action, praxis and application
strings.data.taxonomy.realizationDesc: One category embodies or realizes another
strings.data.taxonomy.recognitionDesc: A category is constituted through recognition of another (Anerkennung)
strings.data.taxonomy.reflectionDesc: A category is turned toward itself or its own ground
strings.data.taxonomy.socialDesc: Categories of society, collectivity and social bonds
strings.data.taxonomy.sufficientConditionDesc: The presence of the first category guarantees the second
strings.data.taxonomy.temporalDesc: A relation of precedence, succession or simultaneity
strings.data.taxonomy.theologicalDesc: Categories of the divine, the sacred and religious experience

strings.landingPage.featureSynthesisText1: From a seed — a question, thesis or intuition — and selected philosophical traditions,
strings.landingPage.featureSynthesisText2: a structured document is built: goals and method, portraits of the participants,
strings.landingPage.featureSynthesisText3: tensions, critical analysis. Six synthesis methods, three levels — from
strings.landingPage.featureSynthesisText4: comparative to generative, four depths of elaboration.
strings.landingPage.heroText: PhiloSynth assembles a new philosophical concept from a seed and selected traditions: it builds a document with sections, extracts categories into a graph, formulates theses and a glossary, conducts a critical analysis — and stores the result so that it can be edited in place, regenerated in a cascade, taken into the next synthesis and opened to others.
strings.landingPage.noPublicConcepts: There are no public concepts yet — yours may be the first.
strings.landingPage.plansText: You can work in three ways: with your own Anthropic key (zero cost for the service), by subscription with monthly quotas, or from the balance — top-up via Stripe, charged at the request's cost price with the service markup. The cost of each synthesis is shown before launch and in the footer of the finished document.

strings.layout.header.heroText: A platform for automated synthesis, analysis and formalization of philosophical concepts based on selected philosophical traditions. Generation of category graphs with interactive 3D/2D visualization, theses, dialogues, historical contextualization and critical analysis — in the form of a single structured document.
